newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB chiefs released pending trial.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB chiefs released pending trial.

text.p: The chairman and chief executive of the Czech bank IPB a.s. Jiri Tesar and his deputy Libor Prochazka were released from jail on Tuesday pending a trial on embezzlement charges, bank spokesman Jan Rezek said.
"They should be here (in the bank) tomorrow morning," Rezek told Reuters, adding that he expected them to make a statement after they take their positions again.
The two executives were arrested on April 29 and charged with embezzlement in connection with a real estate transaction involving the bank's purchase of a building in downtown Prague.
IPB's board of directors and supervisory board both backed the officials saying neither Tesar nor Prochazka violated any law or internal regulations of the bank.

The Czech news agency CTK quoted Prague state attorney Jan Krivanek as saying on Tuesday that the reasons for keeping the financial leaders in jail, including any potential influencing of witnesses, have ended.

IPB is the third largest Czech bank by charter capital. The government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), holds a 31.5 percent stake in IPB, bringing the state's total holding to 36 percent together with post service Ceska Posta.

The state holding is scheduled to be sold off in the middle of the year and ING Bank and Japan's Nomura are frontrunners on the shortlist of buyers, being drawn up by U.S. based investment bank Salomon Brothers.
The NPF has said that the police investigation should not affect the privatisation process.
A Czech-registered company Nutshell s.r.o., whose director Eduard Onderka is also the Czech representative of Nomura, holds a 9.8 percent in IPB.
